==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|thrō|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/θɹəʊ/|[θɾ̪̊əʊ]}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-throe.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{enPR|thrō|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/θɹoʊ/|[θɾ̪̊oʊ]}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-throw.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-au-throw.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{homophones|en|throe}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊ|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*terh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|throwen}}, {{m|enm|thrawen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þrāwan|t=to turn, twist}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þrāan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þrēaną|t=to twist, turn}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*terh₁-|t=to rub, rub by twisting, twist, turn}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|thraw|t=to twist, turn, throw}}, {{cog|fy|triuwe|t=to push}}, {{cog|nl|draaien|t=to turn}}, {{cog|nds|draien}}, {{m|nds|dreien|t=to turn (in a lathe)}}, {{cog|de|drehen|t=to turn}}.

{{displaced|en|sl=1|warp}} as the word for hurling and was {{displaced|en|nocap=1|sl=1|by=1|warp}} as the word for twisting.

The use in computing comes from the fact, that in programming languages a statement reporting an error interrupts normal processing and sends an error object up the function calling stack until a handling statement intercepts it. Thus an “object” is “thrown” and “flies” until it is “caught”.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|+|+|threw,~ed<l:nonstandard>|n,~ed<l:nonstandard>,threw<l:nonstandard>}}
[[File:Le lanceur de coco.jpg|thumb|upright|A man '''throws''' a coconut on a beach in [[Ivory Coast]] (1) ]]

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[hurl]]; to release (an [[object]]) with some [[force]] from one’s hands, an apparatus, etc. so that it moves [[rapidly]] through the [[air]].
#: {{syn|en|bung|cast|fling|hurl|Thesaurus:throw}}
#: {{co|en|'''throw''' a shoe; '''throw''' a javelin}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=When this conversation was repeated in detail within the hearing of the young woman in question, and undoubtedly for his benefit, Mr. Trevor '''threw''' shame to the winds and scandalized the Misses Brewster then and there by proclaiming his father to have been a country storekeeper.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[eject]] or cause to fall off.
#: {{co|en|the horse '''threw''' its rider}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|II|i|passage=There the snake '''throws''' her enamelled skin.}}
#: {{syn|en|eject|throw [[off]]}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To move to another [[position]] or [[condition]]; to [[displace]].
#: {{syn|en|displace|relocate}}
#: {{co|en|'''throw''' the switch}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=17|passage=This time was most dreadful for Lilian. '''Thrown''' on her own resources and almost penniless, she maintained herself and paid the rent of a wretched room near the hospital by working as a charwoman, sempstress, anything. In a moment she had dropped to the level of a casual labourer.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|ceramics}} To make (a [[pot]]) by shaping [[clay]] as it turns on a [[wheel]].
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2009-01-19|author=Linda Franz|title=Basic Pottery Making: All the Skills and Tools You Need to Get Started|publisher=Stackpole Books|isbn=9780811741859
|text=Through practice, you’ll learn how to add the right amount of water as you '''throw''' a pot, and your fingers will feel when the pot has reached the proper thickness.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|cricket|of a [[bowler]]}} To [[deliver]] (the ball) [[illegally]] by [[straighten]]ing the [[bowling]] arm during delivery.
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing}} To send (an {{ll|en|error|id=failure in computing}}) to an [[exception]]-handling mechanism in order to [[interrupt]] normal [[processing]].
#: {{ux|en|If the file is read-only, the method '''throws''' an invalid-operation exception.}}
# {{lb|en|sports|video games}} To intentionally [[lose]] a game.
#: {{syn|en|take a dive}}
#: {{ux|en|The tennis player was accused of taking bribes to '''throw''' the match.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=August 1 2012|author=Peter Walker; Haroon Siddique|publisher=Guardian Unlimited|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/sport/2012/aug/01/london-2012-badminton-disqualified-olympics?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT758I2|title=Eight Olympic badminton players disqualified for 'throwing games'
|passage=Four pairs of women's doubles badminton players, including the Chinese top seeds, have been ejected from the Olympic tournament for trying to '''throw''' matches in an effort to secure a more favourable quarter-final draw.}}
# {{lb|en|sports|transitive}} (of a game where one’s role is throwing something) To [[perform]] in a specified way in (a match).
#: {{ux|en|The pitcher '''threw''' a perfect game.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To [[confuse]] or [[mislead]].
#: {{ux|en|The deliberate red herring '''threw''' me at first.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Jan Blackstone-Ford|title=The Custody Solutions Sourcebook| page=196| passage=“Jann, why does he hate me so much?” That question '''threw''' me. I was expecting a lunatic yelling profanities.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To [[send]] [[hastily]] or [[desperately]].
#: {{ux|en|Their sergeant '''threw''' the troops into pitched battle.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[imprison]].
#: {{ux|en|The magistrate ordered the suspect to be '''thrown''' into jail.}}
#* {{RQ:Mary Shelley Frankenstein||text=The plot of Felix was quickly discovered, and De Lacey and Agatha were '''thrown''' into prison.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1993|author=Margaret McKee; Fred Chisenhall|title=Beale black & blue: life and music on black America’s main street|page=30
|passage=The standard method of dealing with an addict was to arrest him, '''throw''' him into a cell, and leave him until the agonizing pangs of withdrawal were over.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[organize]] an [[event]], especially a [[party]].
#: {{ux|en|She was known for '''throwing''' the craziest parties in college.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1979|journal=Working Mother|month=July|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=SWEEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA72&dq=%22throw+a+party%22&hl=en&ei=KGUeTbvyA426hAfw6OC3Dg&sa=X&oi=book_result&ct=result&resnum=10&ved=0CFkQ6AEwCTgK#v=onepage&q=%22throw%20a%20party%22&f=false|page=72
|passage=Should you be interested, for whatever reason, it will tell you how to '''throw''' a party for your 40-year-old husband or your 100-year-old great-grandmother. It also describes games that can be played at various kinds of parties{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[roll]] (a [[die]] or [[dice]]).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1844|translator=Samuel Laing|author=w:Snorri Sturluson|title=Heimskringla
|passage=The kings came to the agreement between themselves that they would cast lots by the dice to determine who should have this property, and that he who threw the highest should have the district. The Swedish king threw two sixes, and said King Olaf need scarcely '''throw'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause a certain number on the [[die]] or [[dice]] to be shown after rolling it.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1844|translator=Samuel Laing|author=w:Snorri Sturluson|title=Heimskringla
|passage=The kings came to the agreement between themselves that they would cast lots by the dice to determine who should have this property, and that he who '''threw''' the highest should have the district. The Swedish king '''threw''' two sixes, and said King Olaf need scarcely throw.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|bridge}} To [[discard]].
# {{lb|en|martial arts}} To [[lift]] or [[unbalance]] one’s opponent and then bring him back down to the [[ground]], especially into a [[position]] behind the [[thrower]].
#* {{RQ:Eddison Worm|page=25|passage=So they stood up, and wrastled another while in silence. Soon the King made trial once again of the fall whereby he had sought to '''throw''' him in the first bout, twisting suddenly his right side against Goldry, and catching with his leg Goldry’s leg, and therewith leaning against him with main force.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To change (one’s voice) in order to give the illusion that the voice is that of someone else, or coming from a different place.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To show sudden [[emotion]], especially anger.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1991|author=Janet L. Davies; Ellen Hastings Janosik|title=Mental health and psychiatric nursing: a caring approach
|passage=Bill runs into the kitchen and tells Dad that Erik is '''throwing''' a tantrum. He tells Bill to go back and watch his program and to ignore his brother. Fifteen minutes later, Erik is still screaming{{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:New York|date=19 Aug 1996|volume=29|number=32|title=Entertaining Mrs Stone
|passage=In 1975, pregnant with the second of her three children, she '''threw''' a hissy fit to get on a trip to Boston for elected officials.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[project]] or [[send forth]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make a [[shape]] or [[gesture]] with the [[hand]]s.
#: {{ux|en|I '''threw''' scissors but she '''threw''' rock and beat me.}}
#: {{ux|en|The teens were '''throwing''' gang signs.}}
# To [[put on]] [[hastily]]; to [[spread]] [[carelessly]]. {{attention|en|I don't see that "spreading" could be any meaning of "putting on". Was it meant to be a second meaning?}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1726|chapter=Book III|title={{w|Odyssey|The Odyssey}}|by=w:Homer|author=[[w:Alexander Pope|Alexander, transl. Pope]]|line=596|newversion=republished in|title2=The Complete Poetical Works of Alexander Pope|location2=Boston, New York|publisher2=Houghton, Mifflin and Company|year2=1902|page2=543|pageurl2=https://archive.org/details/completepoetical00pope/page/543|passage=O’er his fair limbs a flowery vest he '''threw'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To prepare (a [[cocktail]]) by pouring liquid between [[shaker]]s from a height.
#: {{ux|en|The barman taught me how to '''throw''' a cocktail.}}
# To twist two or more filaments of (silk, etc.) so as to form one thread; to twist together, as singles, in a direction contrary to the twist of the singles themselves; sometimes applied to the whole class of operations by which silk is prepared for the weaver.
# {{lb|en|baseball|slang|of a team, a manager, etc.}} To [[select]] (a [[pitcher]]); to assign a pitcher to a given role (such as [[starter]] or [[reliever]]).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Michael T. Lynch, Jr.|title=It Ain’t So: A Might-Have-Been History of the White Sox in 1919 and Beyond|pageurl=https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=QliQBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA63&dq=%22throw+lefty%7Crighty%22&hl=en&sa=X&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q=%22throw%20lefty%7Crighty%22&f=false|page=63|isbn=0786441895
|passage=I have a minor quibble with Gleason’s decision to '''throw''' Lefty Williams in Game Eight with the Series in the balance.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To install (a bridge).
#*: {{...}} across the rapid smaragdus-green waters, pouring onward into the country, are '''thrown''' three bridges {{...}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|Scotland|Northern England}} To [[twist]] or [[turn]].
#: {{co|en|a '''thrown''' nail}}
# {{lb|en|American football}} {{synonym of|en|pass}}.
# {{lb|en|transitive|of a punch or boxing combination}} To [[deliver]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1941|journal=Newsweek|volume=18|page=54|url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Newsweek/lFAQAAAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=%22Throw+a+punch%22&dq=%22Throw+a+punch%22&printsec=frontcover
|passage={{...}} not only did I not want to '''throw''' a punch at him, I wanted to give him a solid silver token of thanks {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|veterinary medicine}} Of animals: to [[give birth]] to (young).
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1916|journal=Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association|volume=49
|passage=At the end of the normal gestation period the cow '''threw''' two calf mummies as large as cats.}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# The act of throwing something.
#: {{ux|en|With an accurate '''throw''', he lassoed the cow.}}
#: {{ux|en|What a great '''throw''' by the quarterback!}}
#: {{ux|en|The gambler staked everything on one '''throw''' of the dice.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Hans-Wolfgang Loidl|title=Trends in Functional Programming|volume=5|page=62
|passage=If the expression is a '''throw''', we ''unwind the stack'' seeking a handler expression.}}
# {{lb|en|martial arts}} A [[move]] in which one [[lift]]s or [[unbalance]]s one’s [[opponent]] and then [[bring]]s him down to the [[ground]].
# One’s ability to throw.
#: {{ux|en|He’s always had a pretty decent '''throw'''.}}
# The [[distance]] [[travel]]led by something thrown.
#: {{coi|en|a [[stone's throw|stone's '''throw''']]}}
#* {{RQ:Eddison Worm|page=104|passage=Only on the north-east may aught save a winged thing come at the castle, across a smooth grass-grown saddle less than a stone’s '''throw''' in width.}}
# {{rfv-sense|en}} The [[flight]] of a thrown object.
# {{senseid|en|displacement}} A [[distance]] [[travel]]led in general; [[displacement]].
#: {{co|en|the '''throw''' of the piston}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1947|author=James Jerome Gibson|journal=Motion Picture Testing and Research|issue=7|page=49
|passage=The visibility of the screen image is affected by the length of '''throw''' of the projector, the type of projector, the intensity of the projector lamp, and the type of the screen.}}
# A piece of [[fabric]] used to cover a bed, sofa or other soft furnishing.
#: {{syn|en|throwover|throw blanket}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A single [[instance]], [[occurrence]], [[venture]], or [[chance]].
#: {{ux|en|Football tickets are expensive at fifty bucks a '''throw'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|part of a crankshaft}} Any of the [[projection]]s integral to a [[crankshaft]] that receive or impart [[cranking]] motion from a [[connecting rod]] or similar component.
# {{senseid|en|lathe}} {{lb|en|historical}} A hand-operated [[lathe]], especially a small lathe used by [[clockmaker]]s.
